problem: Large language models struggle with reasoning on constrained parameters, and existing looped transformers waste computation by revising already-correct token predictions in later iterations.
approach: Think-at-Hard (TaH) uses a lightweight neural decider to selectively trigger latent iterations only for tokens likely to be incorrect, combined with depth-aware LoRA modules and duo-causal attention for cross-iteration information flow.
contribution: TaH outperforms always-iterate baselines by 3.8-4.4% with identical parameters while skipping iterations on 93% of tokens, and exceeds single-iteration Qwen3 baselines by 3.0-3.8%.

problem: Classifier-Free Guidance for diffusion models causes oversaturation, texture artifacts, and structural collapse at high guidance scales due to off-manifold sampling trajectories.
approach: Manifold-Optimal Guidance (MOG) reformulates guidance as a local optimal control problem that performs geometry-aware Riemannian updates correcting manifold drift, with Auto-MOG providing adaptive schedule tuning.
contribution: MOG yields superior fidelity and alignment compared to baselines with virtually no added computational overhead.

problem: Differential privacy training for LLMs requires fast gradient clipping with prohibitive memory overhead O(B·min(T², d²)) that scales poorly with model width and context length.
approach: DP-SGD-RC uses stochastic trace estimation methods (Hutchinson's estimator and Hutch++) to reduce per-sample gradient norm estimation overhead while maintaining competitive noise multipliers.
contribution: DP-SGD-RC matches baseline utility while significantly reducing memory and compute on long-context LLM fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Quantum algorithms for linear systems (HHL) and quantum recommender systems were thought to provide exponential speedup, but quantum-inspired classical algorithms have reduced most to polynomial, leaving uncertainty about achievable quantum advantages.
approach: The paper establishes a provable exponential separation by analyzing the quantum algorithm for solving well-conditioned linear systems with sparse rows and columns, proving quantum-inspired classical methods cannot match.
contribution: First provable exponential separation between quantum and quantum-inspired classical algorithms for a natural machine learning task (linear systems with sparse structure).

problem: Hyperbolic metric learning focuses primarily on the Poincaré model, which has curved geodesics misaligned with linear projections in modern neural networks.
approach: Investigate the Klein model of hyperbolic geometry with straight-line geodesics, formalizing a framework using Einstein gyrovector operations to derive a numerically stable hyperbolic metric learning approach.
contribution: Klein model achieves competitive performance on fine-grained image classification while serving as an efficient geometric alternative to the Poincaré model without increasing parameter complexity.

problem: Neural symbolic regression generates tree-structured expressions but existing neural methods linearize trees into tokens, obscuring hierarchy and complicating constraint enforcement.
approach: GCN-SR generates expressions in explicit tree-aligned form using Symbolic Perfect Binary Trees (SPBTs) for fixed-topology scaffolding, with Similarity-Weighted Policy Gradient (SWPG) incorporating genetic programming refinement.
contribution: GCN-SR consistently improves exact recovery over strong neural and hybrid baselines on symbolic regression benchmarks under matched evaluation budgets.

problem: Large multimodal models integrate vision and language but their internal representations remain opaque and interpretability through explicit logic is missing.
approach: Use neuro-fuzzy approach with fuzzy rules computing activation firing strengths that are defuzzified to extract distinct interpretable multimodal concepts.
contribution: Framework produces semantically coherent and interpretable multimodal concepts with validated utility for interpreting test samples and disentangling visual-textual grounding.

problem: Multimodal reasoning models generate long reasoning traces but verifying that visual reasoning is grounded in image evidence requires costly causal methods or lacks causal validity.
approach: Amortized framework learns to estimate causal effects of semantic regions from attention features, enabling real-time visual attribution streaming without exhaustive backward passes.
contribution: Achieves faithfulness comparable to exhaustive causal methods while enabling live attribution streaming as the model reasons across five benchmarks and four thinking models.

problem: Machine learning models for geographic data distribute representational capacity uniformly globally, struggling at fine-grained local resolutions needed for disease/ecological/economic applications.
approach: Geographic location encoder built from spherical Slepian functions that concentrate capacity inside a region-of-interest, with hybrid Slepian-Spherical Harmonic encoder for global context.
contribution: Slepian encodings outperform baselines on five tasks (classification, regression, image-augmented prediction) while retaining pole-safety and spherical-distance preservation.

problem: SWE-Bench leaderboard approaches saturation at 78.80% but many 'solved' patches are semantically incorrect, passing only due to weak test suites.
approach: SWE-ABS strengthens test suites through coverage-driven augmentation using program slicing and mutation-driven adversarial testing to expose semantic blind spots.
contribution: Strengthens 50.2% of instances (25.1× improvement) and rejects 19.78% of previously passing patches, dropping top agent score from 78.80% to 62.20% and reshuffling leaderboard.

problem: Stochastic programming is challenged by epistemic uncertainty when critical probability distributions are poorly characterized due to data scarcity.
approach: Minimize an upper confidence bound (UCB) on expected random cost using the Average Percentile Upper Bound (APUB), a statistically rigorous construct serving as robust risk metric.
contribution: APUB provides asymptotically correct and consistent framework with practical solution methods (bootstrap approximation, L-shaped method) fortifying decisions against epistemic uncertainty.

problem: Video understanding models lack deep reasoning and knowledge integration, relying on textual shortcuts rather than genuine visual comprehension.
approach: VideoKR corpus with 315K reasoning examples over 145K CC-licensed expert-domain videos, using human-in-the-loop skill-oriented pipeline targeting progressively deeper reasoning.
contribution: Models post-trained on VideoKR via SFT→GRPO outperform prior approaches on knowledge-intensive video reasoning while remaining competitive on general video understanding.

problem: Visual generative models acquire rich knowledge during training but existing representations remain external and cannot directly exploit this knowledge for compact storage.
approach: Implicit visual representation framework encodes signals as functions parametrized by low-rank adaptations attached to frozen generative models, hashable to compact vectors.
contribution: Implicit representations achieve strong perceptual video compression at extremely low bitrates and enable inference-time scaling and control, bridging visual compression and generation.

problem: Federated continual learning overlooks spatial and temporal information inherent in real-world settings, leading to suboptimal model performance.
approach: GFedCL constructs spatial- and temporal-aware relational graphs with attention mechanisms combined with generative adversarial learning for synthetic data generation.
contribution: GFedCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated continual learning methods with 27.95% improvement on TinyImageNet while preserving privacy.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) merging from multiple trained LoRAs suffers from severe parameter interference causing destructive collisions in shared parameter space.
approach: Subspace Signal Routing (SSR) resolves interference by routing internal signals using inverse correlation matrix decorrelation and directional guide matrices into task-specific subspaces.
contribution: SSR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods with proven mathematical optimality via OLS solution and streaming algorithm with reduced memory overhead.

problem: Audio-visual deepfake detection relies on cross-modal inconsistencies but singing weakens this coupling through rhythmic vocalization, causing significant performance degradation.
approach: Text-guided Audio-Visual Forgery Detection (T-AVFD) framework learns generalizable authenticity patterns by aligning facial features with multi-granularity textual descriptions.
contribution: T-AVFD shows consistent improvements over baselines on multiple talking head datasets and the new Singing Head DeepFake (SHDF) dataset with strong robustness.

problem: Symmetry discovery for stochastic dynamical systems has been largely unexplored, yet Lie-point symmetries are valuable for improving model robustness and interpretability.
approach: LieStoNet learns neural surrogates for drift and diffusion, then discovers projectable generators by enforcing SDE determining equations with Lie algebra axiom regularization.
contribution: LieStoNet recovers generators consistent with ground-truth symmetry algebra on canonical SDEs, providing interpretable symmetry discovery for noisy dynamics.

problem: Tabular Language Models are claimed to achieve strong generalization but systematic re-evaluation reveals performance inflated by evaluation artifacts and data contamination.
approach: Systematic re-evaluation of Tabula-8B on 165 UniPredict datasets, analyzing task contamination, train-test overlap, and instruction-tuning contribution.
contribution: Binary/categorical classification achieve near-zero median lift; instruction-tuning recovers 92.2% of performance, suggesting claimed generalization reflects evaluation artifacts.

problem: Autoregressive visual generation is slow, requiring thousands of per-token generation steps that severely constrain practical adoption.
approach: Speculative Coupled Decoding (SCD) extends Speculative Jacobi Decoding with information-theoretic coupling to stabilize draft trajectories by maximizing probability of identical tokens across iterations.
contribution: Achieves up to 4.2× speedup in image generation and 13.6× in video generation without quality degradation or draft model training.

problem: Logistic regression with high-dimensional data exhibits bias and variance that depend on signal strength, but accurate signal strength estimation methods are lacking.
approach: Data-splitting strategy to estimate signal strength, analyzing exact asymptotics of M-estimators with data-driven non-decomposable regularizers adapted to true covariance.
contribution: Provides theoretically justified method for signal strength estimation in high-dimensional logistic regression through data-splitting and regularization.

problem: Transferring capabilities learned with privileged information to policies without it at inference remains challenging, especially when reasoning is hidden in closed-source systems.
approach: π-Distill trains a PI-conditioned teacher and unconditioned student simultaneously within shared-parameter model, enabling teacher to learn using PI while mitigating distribution shift.
contribution: π-Distill matches or outperforms industry-standard pipelines with full Chain-of-Thought supervision using only action-based privileged information.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting training with geometric priors is challenging when geometric supervision is spatially incomplete and uneven in large-scale outdoor scenes.
approach: EnerGS models partially observable geometry as continuous energy field providing soft geometric guidance rather than hard constraints, avoiding solution space restriction.
contribution: Consistently improves photometric quality and geometric stability under sparse multi-view and monocular settings while mitigating overfitting.

problem: State space models using HiPPO matrices lack continuous-limit analysis and explicit solution formulas, limiting theoretical understanding.
approach: Propose Continuized-HiPPO Operator as continuous limit of HiPPO Matrix, enabling analysis of eigenvalue asymptotics and derivation of explicit solutions.
contribution: Provides eigenvalue analysis and explicit solution formula for linear state space models based on continuous HiPPO operator.

problem: Regularized MDPs improve RL stability but theoretical analyses focus on standard settings, leaving robust RL understanding incomplete.
approach: Doubly regularized MDP framework combines policy and dynamics regularizations for robust learning, with optimism-based online algorithm providing finite-sample regret guarantees.
contribution: First finite-sample regret guarantees for doubly regularized MDPs in tabular and linear settings, matching robust MDP efficiency while enabling soft policies.

problem: Real-world AI assistance requires robust Theory of Mind but faces challenges in online inference with multiple hypotheses, efficiency, and lack of ground-truth annotations.
approach: MindZero uses self-supervised RL to train MLLMs for mental reasoning by rewarding hypotheses that maximize action likelihood via model-based planning.
contribution: MindZero outperforms model-based baselines in accuracy and efficiency, showing mental reasoning can be learned as self-supervised skill without annotations.

problem: Video LLMs using autoregressive paradigm face dual efficiency bottleneck: unidirectional attention limits spatiotemporal aggregation and serial decoding restricts generation efficiency.
approach: VidLaDA uses diffusion language models with bidirectional attention for comprehensive spatiotemporal modeling and parallel token decoding, with MARS-Cache pruning redundancy.
contribution: Rivals state-of-the-art autoregressive baselines while outperforming diffusion baselines, with MARS-Cache delivering over 12× speedup without accuracy loss.

problem: Text-to-image generative models achieve high semantic alignment but struggle to synthesize diverse images from given prompts.
approach: Geometry-Aware Spherical Sampling (GASS) decomposes diversity in CLIP embeddings along text and orthogonal directions, controlling both prompt-dependent and prompt-independent variation.
contribution: GASS increases geometric projection spread for both axes, improving diversity while maintaining fidelity and semantic alignment across multiple frozen T2I backbones.

problem: Medical image segmentation requires balancing global context with efficiency, but self-attention suffers from prohibitive quadratic complexity O((HW)² C).
approach: S2M-Net uses Spectral-Spatial Token Mixing (SSTM) achieving O(HWC²) complexity through efficient frequency-domain processing and spatial gating.
contribution: Achieves best performance on 14 of 15 datasets with statistically significant improvements on 7 challenging tasks and clinically meaningful gains on 8 benchmarks.

problem: Poster generation requires integrating visual aesthetics and information hierarchy, but text-to-image models lack editability and struggle with text rendering.
approach: PosterAgent reformulates poster creation as agentic workflow with iterative refinement inspired by human designers, using Stage-Aware RL decoupling draft and refinement phases.
contribution: PosterAgent significantly outperforms strong baselines, validating agentic systems' potential for enabling self-correction in professional graphic design.

problem: GNN explainability methods extract sparse single-scale key subgraphs but miss multi-level semantics and suffer from unstable, noise-sensitive optimization.
approach: MSExplainer couples multi-scale subgraph consistency guidance with single-scale adaptive learning under parameter-sharing, simultaneously extracting multi-scale and complementary subgraphs.
contribution: MSExplainer outperforms prior methods in explanation accuracy and fidelity with theoretically proven upper bound advantage while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Large language models produce toxic text even for benign inputs, but existing detoxification approaches rely on costly retraining or learned components.
approach: Test-time procedure uses zeroth-order optimization to approximate gradient of completion toxicity with respect to input embeddings, steering generation toward less toxic continuations.
contribution: Delivers robust toxicity reductions across models achieving best overall toxicity-quality trade-off without requiring training or intermediate computation access.

problem: Adaptive LoRA merging methods show improvements in controlled settings but their effectiveness with wild LoRAs from model repositories remains unexplored.
approach: Empirical study recycling nearly 1,000 user-contributed LoRAs from Hugging Face Hub, evaluating adaptive and non-adaptive merging methods including new methodology.
contribution: Adaptive merging improves performance over base model but provides limited benefit over training new LoRA; random LoRAs yield similar performance to curated pools.

problem: Last-iterate convergence for stochastic monotone variational inequalities lacks anytime guarantees despite relevance to uncoupled learning dynamics.
approach: Analyze regularized gradient (RG) and regularized optimistic gradient (ROG) methods, establishing anytime last-iterate convergence rates in terms of squared gap function.
contribution: RG attains O(t^{-2/5}) and ROG achieves variance-adaptive O(σ^{4/5} t^{-2/5} + t^{-1}), providing guarantees without knowing horizon.

problem: Cache-based test-time adaptation for VLMs introduces latency overhead as cache grows with classes and performs suboptimally with insufficient cache samples.
approach: Prototype-Based Test-Time Adaptation (PTA) uses class-specific knowledge prototypes weighted by zero-shot confidence, accumulating knowledge from test samples without cache overhead.
contribution: PTA improves CLIP accuracy from 65.64% to 69.38% on 10 cross-domain benchmarks while retaining 92% inference speed, state-of-the-art on 15 image and 4 point cloud benchmarks.

problem: Object insertion methods achieve high visual quality but treat insertion as 2D inpainting without explicit 3D pose control, limiting practical applicability.
approach: DIRECT decomposes insertion into appearance, geometry, and context guidance injected through separate pathways, enabling pose-controllable insertion via interactive 3D proxy manipulation.
contribution: DIRECT outperforms previous methods in both geometric controllability and visual quality with automated data construction pipeline.

problem: Test-time scaling via token sampling requires temperature tuning trading off diversity against stability, with fine-grained MoE offering unexplored routing alternatives.
approach: Expert-Sample preserves high-confidence expert selections while injecting controlled stochasticity into uncertain tail of router scores, enabling diverse generation.
contribution: Expert-Sample consistently improves pass@n and verification-based accuracy; on Qwen3-30B pass@32 rises from 85.4% to 91.9% with Best-of-N verification reaching 62.6%.

problem: Small language models fail to scale with task complexity on deep search and coding, with unclear routing strategies for leveraging heterogeneous agents.
approach: Strategy Auctions for Workload Efficiency (SALE) enables agents to bid with strategic plans scored by cost-value mechanism with shared auction memory for per-task routing.
contribution: SALE reduces reliance on largest agent by 52%, lowers overall cost by 35%, and improves pass@1 with negligible overhead, enabling effective small-agent scaling.

problem: Optimal mechanisms for private mean estimation in shuffle model remain unexplored despite differences from local differential privacy settings.
approach: Formulate post-shuffling mechanism design as explicit optimization using shuffle index, establishing lower bounds on achievable mean squared error.
contribution: Constructs asymptotically optimal mechanism achieving privacy-utility trade-off nearly identical to central Gaussian mechanism.

problem: Medical images show sparse visual evidence for clinical decision-making but existing VLM-RL approaches don't prune irrelevant visual tokens before reasoning.
approach: ViToS dual-stream RL framework trains one policy for both visual token pruning and question answering, solving coupled learning via cross-feedback sequential optimization.
contribution: ViToS reduces visual tokens to 77% of original while achieving 108.27% relative performance on Lingshu-7B and 104.16% on HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B.

problem: Long-term time series forecasting emphasizes architectural complexity over fundamental forecasting structures, leading to overengineering and poor generalization.
approach: ReNF reformulates LTSF using Variance Reduction Hypothesis and Boosted Direct Output paradigm hybridizing Auto-Regressive and Direct Output with parameter smoothing.
contribution: Direct temporal MLP outperforms recent complex state-of-the-art models on nearly all benchmarks without intricate inductive biases.
